kind: A screen by slope on the server's test bed (two seeds, 6,000 and 24,000 updates) and a full-size pilot (one seed, 24,000 updates): balanced synapses (--balanced-synapses), which centre what every read, plain cell and output neuron hears.
why: full_size_layout_in_floats.json: the stack's pool in place of every LayerNorm costs the Transformer 0.0691, the largest part of the layout's distance found so far. The pool divides by the stream's activity but takes no mean out. In cortex excitation and inhibition onto a neuron balance, so that it answers the pattern of its inputs and not their level. Balanced synapses do that exactly in whole ticks: every synapse of a read's probe, tag and payload neurons, of a plain cell and of an output neuron is held at the neuron's mean synapse less (over each copy of the stream that late fibres bring), so each neuron's synapses sum to within half a tick per synapse of zero, and a level added to every channel moves no charge. The charge stays exact (the balanced ticks bound the sums and the synaptic scaling), the parameters are the same, the pool still divides. full_size_centring_in_floats.json (the Transformer with a centred pool) runs tonight and says whether centring is the pool's price.

arms.bal (test bed): sched/bin/arm.sh stack --lr 1.2e-3 --seed 2000X [--steps 6000] --balanced-synapses: the delayed bed with balanced synapses; 5,249,060 parameters, as the bed
arms.fs-loop6-lift-bal (full size): sched/bin/full.sh stack fs-loop6-lift-bal --lr 6e-4 --stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --balanced-synapses: the lifted loop with balanced synapses; 34,810,900 parameters, as fs-loop6-lift

base: Test bed: bed24-lr12-s1 1.486381, bed24-lr12-s2 1.492556, rd-base-6k-s1 1.621562, rd-base-6k-s2 1.628309. Full size: fs-loop6-lift 1.300729 (same recipe, seed and measure).
runs: bal-6k-s1, bal-6k-s2, bal-24k-s1, bal-24k-s2 and fs-loop6-lift-bal on GPU 0, on a new code copy of the commit that records this (v18f, launch-checked on the server's CPU first), queued only if full_size_centring_in_floats.json reads centring or both; if it reads the division, they are not run and a pool that divides by the spread is built instead.
measure: arm.sh's and full.sh's scores (experiments/eval_stream.py on the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams after 8,192 lead bytes, averaged weights), paired with the base of each seed and length (compare_stream_scores.py), split by context (gap_by_piece.py, near 240, far 8,192); the pulses a byte.
reading: Test bed: the shared reading of experiments/read_lead_study.py (--base-long bed24-lr12-s1 bed24-lr12-s2 --base-short rd-base-6k-s1 rd-base-6k-s2 --arm balanced bal-24k-s1 bal-24k-s2 --arm-short balanced bal-6k-s1 bal-6k-s2): a fix for late learning, a constant gain, or a fail. Because the option costs no parameters and no pulses, a mean lead of at least 0.005 after 24,000 updates with both seeds ahead adopts it on the bed. Full size: balanced synapses join the next full-length run if fs-loop6-lift-bal is at least 0.005 better than fs-loop6-lift with the paired interval clear of zero; between 0 and 0.005 better a second seed decides; worse, they stay off at full size whatever the bed shows. The two readings are reported together; the full size decides for full-length runs.
seen_before_recording: full_size_layout_in_floats.json with its result; tests/test_balanced_synapses.py on small stacks (whole ticks summing to nearly zero, a neuron deaf to a level added to every channel, the same spikes however a stream is cut, shrinking by the balanced sizes). No stack with balanced synapses has trained.

decision.change: Not run, as the record says for this case: full_size_centring_in_floats.json read the division (the centred pool still costs the Transformer 0.0636; centring recovers 0.0056). The code stays (--balanced-synapses, aa37176) and may return with a pool that divides by the spread, in a record written then.
